Being new to the area, I found South Park Animal Hospital after reading through many online reviews when my dog developed an ear infection. Choosing a new vet can be stressful, but from the moment we walked in, the staff was incredibly welcoming and kind, which immediately made the experience feel more comfortable.

The hospital itself is very clean, well organized, and has a calm, inviting environment. It feels like a place where both pets and their owners are genuinely cared for. The vet took time to explain everything clearly, which I really appreciated as a new client.

There was a bit of a wait for the prescription after the vet saw my dog, but I wasn’t in a hurry, so it truly didn’t bother me at all. The staff remained attentive during the wait, and the overall experience still felt smooth and positive.

I will definitely be back in the coming months when my dog is due for her shots. Based on my research, this clinic is also fairly affordable, especially considering the quality of care and location. I highly recommend South Park Animal Hospital if you’re looking for a welcoming, trustworthy, and well-run veterinary clinic in a great area of San Francisco.

text.text:
It has been a month since my best friend Toby passed. As difficult as it is for me to write this, my family and I greatly appreciate the effort the staff made to help my dog, Toby.

Toby was family, and for 15.5 years, I was able to cherish every moment being with him until the end.

Despite all the pain he endured, Toby was conscious and had a fighting spirit as he waited for his owner's help. I called SAGE ahead, and when I went to pick up Toby, during the car ride, it felt as though he was talking to me. When he heard my voice, he let out a big sigh, then began whimpering to me, reflecting his pain and relief at seeing me. I was reassuring him the whole ride to the vet, telling Toby he was going to be alright and to push a bit more, and he barked back. I said we made it, boy, and brought him inside. At this point, I put my faith in accepting whatever outcome will be... and Toby passed, he stopped breathing while in the operating room, but somehow got a breath of air again. The nurse saw this and brought him into the room so that my family and I could say our goodbyes. His body was shutting down, his eyes were off balance, neck was broken, and he was gasping for air. It was hard to watch.

A dog is more than just a pet; they are angels, and I was fortunate enough to be with Toby as he was not alone. His last moments were where he showed me his loyalty and unconditional love by turning his head to look at me one last time. Toby closed his mouth, flared his ears forward, and his eyes locked onto mine as his pupils dilated. It was a moment of peace for both of us. It was his way of saying thank you.

It's taken me 2 years to write this, mainly due to grieving. I moved to sf and it was a really hard time mentally and financially on my own. I unexpectedly lost both my Siberian huskies at the same time due to them getting into things while I was away, it was the most devastating loss I've had to go through. Sadly I don't remember the vet and their staff there but I can't thank you enough for the CONTINUOUS compassion they had while I made my way to them.
They gave me my options, were very emphatic on their time line, the chances they had and didn't pressure me into any decision. With their help, and kindness I had to make the hardest decision to let them both go. The staff gave me as much time as I needed, and let me tell you, I needed it. These two were my biggest joy in life and they walked me through it all with so much compassion.

I appreciated them laying out blankets on the floor vs having them lay on the concrete floor or the metal tables. They made it very comfortable for them to both be together in the same room and allow me to lay with them on the blankets.
They walked me through the process with each vile they admitted, took their time when I needed them to stop to hold them and began gaining when I was ready. They were just so compassionate and ensured they passed at the same time together. I will forever be grateful for that level of patience and empathy.

It was heartbreaking seeing staff also tear up, I remember one of the staff mentioning they'd never had to euthanize two huskies at the same time. It was a really hard night for everyone. After it was all done, they gave me the room and were so supportive, they walked me through my options, and even mentioned I could have more time to decide if needed for costs and cremations.

I was so devastated of their sudden passing I asked for two small vials of fur to remember them by and they helped me collect some.

It's taken a very long time but looking back, I'm so thankful for how loving this staff were to a complete stranger. If anyone needs any emergency support or sadly, a place to go to for their loved pets euthanasia, I recommend them.

One thing I didn't know vets/cremation places can do, they can offer you a private cremation (just your pet to be cremated on its own at a higher price, or a different kind where they are cremated with others, I was taken back by that but I can see now why some may opt the cheaper price if they can't afford it, I personally did the private pet cremation one and payed more)
They are also partnered with "Animal Memorial Service" funeral home in Gilroy,CA, and walked me through every step of the way. When Animal Memorial Service dropped my pups urns back to SAGE they called me right away, and I was very pleased with how I felt they went above and beyond. The urn plaque (I do wish it was a screwed on name vs a sticky seal and included the year) but it did have their name and time of passing, it came with a letter certificate when they were cremated, a wooden print of their paws which I didn't expect to get, a ink stamp of their paws (and they emailed me a digital print of their paws when I requested, true to size, which I've since tattooed on me).

Thank you again SAGE Veterinary Center

My partner and I found SF Vet Hospital while looking for dental care for our 11 year old maltipoo/pom who needed extractions. The estimate matched what we received from another vet but what set SF Vet Hospital apart was the care we received from Dr gill and our vet assistants, Jamie and Joy. There were a lot of emotions as we navigated the cost of 11 extractions and surgery on an 11 year old dog. Dr Gill and his team remained patient with us as we asked questions and discussed all of our options.

Jamie talked us through the estimate and gave us a thorough explanation of everything they would be doing. She did not apply pressure and helped us navigate the procedure and related costs with care. We also really appreciated the care we received after the surgery as Dr Gill took us through why he had to remove each tooth and what to expect in recovery.

Right after surgery Dr Gill told us our dog would be a different, happier dog in 2 weeks and we didn't think it was possible as he was already an outgoing happy dog. Now, a few months post surgery - it's obvious Dr Gill was right. This surgery has greatly improved Theo's quality of life - he has more energy, plays more, and is overall more cuddly. We are so thankful for the care we ALL received at SF Vet Hospital and will definitely be recommending and continuing to bring our (now toothless) Theo here.

I brought my dog to this ER because half of her face suddenly became swollen. I was extremely worried that she might have been bitten by a poisonous insect since I had taken her outside the day before.This was clearly an urgent situation.

They took my dog away from me and immediately asked me to pay. Naturally, I thought they had discovered something serious or life-threatening.

When I asked about her condition, they gave me no explanation and simply told me to signed the contract and proceed with the payment.

By the time I asked for an update, my dog had already finished her examination and I had been waiting for over two hours. When I asked how much longer it would take, I was repeatedly told that they did not know.

Later, I was informed that the doctor was busy with other patients and that I would need to wait about another hour.

During that time, I could see how anxious my dog was, so I took her outside briefly to calm her down. We returned exactly one hour later as instructed, only to be told that nothing was ready and no further steps had been taken.

At that point, a kind male nurse noticed how stressed my dog was and offered us a private room, which I appreciated. However, this does not make up for the lack of medical evaluation and communication.

We then waited another 20 minutes before finally speaking with the doctor.

Later, I found out that the only thing they had done was examine her eyes — which turned out to be completely fine. They performed no blood tests, no imaging, and no proper diagnostics, and still could not tell me what caused the swelling.

Their answer was simply: “We don’t know.”

After the consultation, I was told that medication would be prescribed.

I waited another 10 minutes, then went to the front desk to ask when I could pick up the medication — and again, I was told they “didn’t know.”

What shocked me further was being told that if her condition got worse, I could come back for further testing.
As a pet owner, I came here to prevent her condition from worsening — not to wait until it became more dangerous.

They also entered my email address incorrectly, and I had to call twice just to have it corrected.

While I was still at the hospital, I repeatedly asked:
•	When will I receive the invoice?
•	When can I pick up the medication?

I was told they could not provide any timeline.

Eventually, they refunded $180, which I appreciate, but this does not change how distressing and unprofessional the entire experience was.

I left with no clear diagnosis, no proper explanation, no medication, and unnecessary stress for both me and my dog, after paying $500 upfront and waiting for hours.

Thankfully, my dog’s swelling went down on its own the next day.

Emergency care should be about transparency, timely diagnostics, and protecting animals — not creating panic, taking payment first, and offering no answers.

I would not recommend this place to anyone who truly cares about their pet’s safety. Like I  never leave negative reviews for local businesses, because I understand how difficult it is to run one. But this experience crossed a line.

Update after the clinic’s response:

My concern was not the deposit or wait time, but the lack of communication and medical direction.

My dog was taken away and I was asked to pay without being told what was found or what care would be provided. After the exam, I waited over two hours and no one could tell me how much longer it would take. No blood tests or imaging were done, I was given no diagnosis, no treatment plan, and was even told to come back if her condition worsened, which defeats the purpose of emergency care.

I only received my invoice after calling three times, and only then was informed that I was eligible for a refund. To this day, I still have not received my dog’s medical report.

I was prepared for the cost of ER. I was not prepared for the emotional stress of being kept in the dark about my dog’s condition for hours.

I believe it is important for other pet owners to understand what to expect in similar situations.

I am so so thankful for SFAMC for turning this horrible accident into immediate care for Sage during this holiday season.

I have hit my limit with this place. I’ve been in San Francisco for nearly 20 years, and over the years I’ve had to take my dog clients to this vet hospital. I’ve even worked at a dog rescue where I had to be at this vet office every now and again to get the dogs their vaccinations before adoption.

Years ago I had a client whose dog was a patient  at this vets office. She was put on antibiotics for nearly a year. She had blood in her stool all that time. Turns out all she needed was a routine, two minute rectal exam to find the polyps she had that were bleeding. These could’ve turned cancerous in that amount of time. Her people had gone to Mexico and when I arrived to watch her for their vacation, the pups rectum had prolapsed. There was blood everywhere and I had to rush her to the emergency vet. She needed surgery.

Now I have a client who is clearly having dental issues. Even the veterinarian there noticed the pup has a cracked tooth. My clients asked if their dog needed his teeth cleaned three years ago, and the veterinarian said that it would be a waste of money. Now my client’s dog will not chew anything remotely hard, and he just had a check up two months ago. The dog is swallowing his treat chews whole and is nearly choking frequently. At his latest visit, the veterinarian there said he his teeth were fine again. The pup likely needs tooth extractions. Luckily, they took my advice and are getting a second opinion. Go to a different veterinary clinic if you need good care for your pets.

I really appreciate organizations like SPCA that offer straightforward, honest care and support for their community.

text.text:
We have been taking our dog to Modern Animal since he was 3 months old, across multiple locations, and it has been sad  to watch the quality of care decline to the point where we are now completely done with this chain.

Our most recent experience at Modern Animal Russian Hill was the breaking point. We drove in from Berkeley for a follow up after an emergency hospital visit. The clinic’s initial plan was to have us drop him off, put him in a kennel for three hours, and give him strong sedatives before we even had a proper, transparent conversation about whether that level of sedation was necessary or safe for him. Baloo has active medical issues, so this plan felt risky and careless. No one clearly explained why heavy sedation was needed, what drug they would use, or what alternatives existed, such as lighter sedation, a shorter stay, or us being present with him.

What made it even worse is that we never even met the vet, Dr Chiara Tice. After driving all the way from Berkeley, every part of this plan was communicated indirectly through staff. There was no direct conversation with the doctor to walk us through the reasoning, answer questions, or tailor the plan based on what we already knew from the emergency visit. That lack of access and transparency was a huge red flag.

The estimate we were given was another major concern. The cost for this follow up at Russian Hill was higher than what we paid at the emergency hospital, because they tried to bundle in more than six hundred dollars of “highly recommended” tests. The ER discharge notes were very clear that Baloo mainly needed a follow up X ray to track improvement, not a full panel of extra diagnostics. As long time clients who were already stressed about our dog, it felt less like medical guidance and more like being upsold.

Based on this experience, I did not feel confident in Dr Chiara Tice’s judgment or approach to managing a more complex case like Baloo’s, especially given that we were not even given the chance to speak with her directly. If she is going to handle cases like this, I strongly feel she should be shadowing a more experienced veterinarian and spending more time in direct consultation with pet owners.

Unfortunately, this is not an isolated incident. At Modern Animal Berkeley, we also had a poor experience with Dr Kristi Dunckel, which again felt like a situation where the vet was out of her depth and unsure how to manage Baloo’s condition. These back to back encounters with what felt like inexperienced vets have completely eroded our trust in this chain.

To be fair, it has not all been negative. About two weeks before the Russian Hill visit, Baloo saw Dr Sindell at Modern Animal Berkeley, and that appointment was much better. It was more thoughtful, more confident, and clearly explained. That contrast is part of the problem. The quality in this chain is very inconsistent. You might get a competent vet like Dr Sindell, or you might end up with someone who feels inexperienced, inaccessible, and quick to default to sedation and expensive testing.

If you are considering Modern Animal, my honest advice as a long time client is to be very cautious, especially with newer vets. Ask detailed questions about any proposed sedation, including why it is needed, what will be used, the dose, risks, and alternatives. Compare their recommendations with your emergency or specialist notes, and do not be afraid to push back if they start stacking “highly recommended” tests that were not indicated. Do not hesitate to walk away if the plan does not feel safe or transparent.

When your pet is sick, you are already stressed and scared. In our recent experiences, especially at Russian Hill and with some visits in Berkeley, Modern Animal did not make things easier, clearer, or calmer. It added confusion, pressure, and worry. After years of loyalty, we no longer trust this chain with Baloo’s care.
We are done with Modern Animal.

Thanks to them, my oldest dog lived to be 20 years old, and even though I lost another, he lived a long life up to 16 years. Today, I have three dogs, and all of them are still under the care of Blue Cross Pet Hospital.

We brought my dog in around 4pm after learning he had ingested some pills earlier in the day while being dog-sat. We clearly explained to the staff that it had been several hours since ingestion. Despite that, they decided to induce vomiting for both my dog and another dog that was with him “just in case,” even though only my dog was showing symptoms (dry gums).

As expected, they recovered only 2 out of 20 pills — the rest had clearly already dissolved. The visit cost over $2,000 for both dogs, and then we were told to go to the emergency hospital because it was “an emergency” and they were closing soon. If the situation truly required emergency care and they knew they couldn’t handle it past 5pm, we should have been directed there immediately instead of going through unnecessary procedures and expenses.

We took our dog to SF Animal Medical Center on Fillmore, where we received far better care, transparency, and communication. The overnight stay and full treatment there actually **cost less than what Urban Pet Hospital charged for one hour of care.**

I later spoke with the doctor at Urban Pet to express my concerns — he said he used his “best judgment” and would look into a possible adjustment to the bill, but it’s now been over a month and I haven’t heard back.

Thankfully, my dog is okay, but the experience was extremely disappointing. I hope the clinic improves transparency and judgment in urgent cases so other pet owners don’t have to go through the same frustration and unnecessary expense.

We were early adopters of Modern Animal in San Francisco. At the beginning, the experience was great. We got a puppy in November 2022, shortly after they opened in August 2022, and everything felt new, modern, and efficient. The 24/7 chat feature was especially helpful. Our puppy needed dental work when her permanent teeth grew in behind her baby teeth, and while the procedure was very expensive, our pet insurance covered most of it and the care itself was fine.

Unfortunately, our experience declined significantly once our dog turned two and we began considering breeding her. We needed progesterone testing, which cost $400. We were told results would be available within 48 hours. For anyone familiar with breeding, progesterone levels can change within hours, and timing during a heat cycle is critical—you can miss the most fertile window by a single day.

Despite multiple follow-ups, we were told the lab was overwhelmed and that the vet was out of the office for 1–2 days. For a company that promotes having many vets available, it was surprising and frustrating that no one else could review and relay the results. We didn’t receive them until three days later, at which point the test was essentially useless and no longer reflected accurate levels. It was a complete waste of money.

We later found a breeder in San Jose who provided the same test for $60 with results in 15 minutes, making Modern Animal’s pricing and delay feel completely unjustifiable. Additionally, their vets demonstrated limited knowledge of reproductive health, including providing us with an incorrect pregnancy ultrasound reading. Our most recent visit was particularly disappointing—the vet was dismissive and lacked basic bedside manner.

Overall, while Modern Animal started strong, the quality of care, responsiveness, and expertise have not kept pace with the high costs. We will be looking for a new veterinary office in 2026.
